answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused price reopening and we face an 18% spend mandate with 14 days to contract renewal. memory_c2 demonstrates that switching to the low-cost vendor achieved sharp unit cost reduction with fast onboarding and reliable invoicing—directly applicable to our current constraint. memory_c4 shows negotiation can recover margin, but the incumbent's explicit refusal eliminates that path. The assembly line runs at 94% capacity, leaving minimal buffer for migration risk, so we cannot defer. Adding a second source (memory_c3 precedent) would split volume and weaken cost leverage when we need maximum reduction. Switching primary supply to the proven low-cost vendor addresses the mandate while leveraging documented operational stability. The verified memory reduces execution risk on the cost and timeline fronts. Standard experiment scale mitigates the line-utilization risk by applying proven incumbent-replacement playbook rather than untested vendor.
